resources.string: How the calf muscle pump helps venous return
Calf muscle pump

Qualitative illustration of one lower-leg vein segment with two valves. Not all veins have valves. Anatomy, valve spacing, motion, and timing are not to scale. The drawing omits other venous routes and is not health advice.
Two valves along a vein
The gastrocnemius and soleus are at the back of the calf. The cutaway shows two valves spaced apart in one representative lower-leg vein.
Calf muscles squeeze the vein
As the calf muscles contract, they compress nearby veins. The illustrated segment narrows as the valve toward the foot closes and the valve toward the heart opens.
The proximal valve lets blood through
Blood moves toward the heart through the open proximal valve. A pressure difference opens the leaflets; the valve does not pump.
The distal valve limits backflow
The leaflets of the distal valve meet, limiting flow back toward the foot while blood can still pass through the proximal valve.
The calf relaxes and the vein refills
As the calf relaxes, the vein widens. In this example, the proximal valve closes and the distal valve reopens, allowing blood from farther down the leg to refill the segment.
